post_result_diagnostic.interpretation: Q3 failed because every identifiable full-history case required exactly one snapshot in both source geometries. Dispersed placement increased the fraction of histories that were observable, not the minimum snapshot count conditional on observability.

interpretation: Equilibrium occupancy had exactly zero activation-history information by construction and audit.
Post-activation transient occupancy could identify exact source-activation history in a large subset of landscapes.
Dispersed source placement did not reduce the minimum snapshot burden conditional on identifiability, refuting Q3; instead it greatly increased the probability that history was identifiable at all.
The provenance-class target was never harder than full history identity and required fewer snapshots in 261 design-rows.
A single t4 snapshot was sufficient in all 579 design-rows where full history was identifiable from the frozen library.
Full activation history remained unresolved in 189 design-rows even after all four transient snapshots.
Later snapshots were not monotonically more informative: in 428 design-rows an earlier snapshot resolved history while t8 alone did not.
claim_boundary: Snapshots are complete structural occupancy maps, not imperfect field surveys.
Snapshot time is graph-step time rather than calibrated calendar time.
History identifiability is limited to the three frozen activation schedules.
The Q3 refutation is retained and is not rescued by the post-result identification-rate diagnostic.
